verses.text: In those days, John the Baptist appeared in the Judean wilderness, preaching:
“Turn back to God, because the Kingdom of Heaven is near!”
John was the one Isaiah the prophet spoke about: “A voice is calling in the wilderness: Prepare the Lord’s way; make his paths straight.”
John wore clothes made of camel’s hair with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
People came out to him from Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan.
They were baptized by him in the Jordan River as they confessed their sins.
When John saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said, “You brood of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming judgment?
Live in a way that shows you’ve truly turned back to God.
Don’t tell yourselves, ‘Abraham is our father.’ I’m telling you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
The ax is already at the trees’ roots. Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
“I baptize you in water as you turn back to God, but someone more powerful than I is coming after me. I’m not even worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
He holds a winnowing fork and will thoroughly clear his threshing floor. He’ll gather the wheat into his barn, but burn the chaff in an unquenchable fire.”
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
John tried to stop him. “I’m the one who needs to be baptized by you, and you’re coming to me?”
Jesus answered, “Let it happen for now. This is the right way for us to fulfill everything God requires.” So John agreed.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, he came up out of the water. The heavens opened, and he saw God’s Spirit coming down like a dove and settling on him.
A voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son. I’m pleased with him.”
